candidates.summary: The pre-halt check reads config.toml, not the running node: a future halt_height cleared without a restart passes the check and the node still halts at it (same text at onyx VALIDATOR.md:147).
candidates.failure_scenario: A validator started with halt_height=C in config.toml, C below the voted halt H. Following section 6 the operator runs `gnoland config get halt_height`, sees C, runs `gnoland config set halt_height 0`, re-checks and gets `0`. The running node applied halt_height once at startup (gno.land/cmd/gnoland/start.go:288-291, SetHaltHeight), so it still halts at C, out of step with the network, and idles until someone notices; validators holding a third of the power doing this stall the chain short of H. Section 6 never says a changed value needs a restart before the halt; only the linked gnoland UPGRADES.md says the node reads it once at startup.
candidates.verify_by: PATH=<bin with gnoland built at df2c4ffca>:$PATH GNOROOT=<tree> bash tests/solo-finder-config-cleared-no-restart.sh 6: expect no halt at 6 once the check prints 0; observe 'config get after clearing: 0' followed by 'halt height 6 reached, node shutting down'.
candidates.evidence: Sandbox run at df2c4ffca, lazy local node: 'config get before start: 6' / 'Halt height configured {"height": 6}' / 'config get after clearing: 0' / 'halt height 6 reached, node shutting down' / 'process alive 5s after the halt' / 'exited 2s after SIGTERM, rc=0'. Recovery is a restart with halt_height 0 before H; the loss is the validator's blocks from C until someone restarts it.

candidates.summary: 'The process does not exit' is stated for every node, but a validator still block-syncing at the halt exits with code 2, so Restart=on-failure does fire (same text at onyx VALIDATOR.md:149).
candidates.failure_scenario: A validator that fell behind is catching up through block sync when the network reaches the governance halt. The halt panic in BeginBlock of halt+1 is not caught there (tm2/pkg/bft/blockchain/reactor.go:536 ApplyBlock; the reactor's only recover, :269, covers respondRoutine), so the process exits with code 2, as gno.land/cmd/gnoland/UPGRADES.md:175 says. systemd Restart=on-failure restarts the old binary, which the after-halt gate refuses below halt_min_version, so the operator meets a restart loop where section 6 told them the supervisor does not fire, and must stop the unit, not only the process, before starting the new version.
candidates.verify_by: Read gno.land/cmd/gnoland/UPGRADES.md:175 and grep -n 'recover()' tm2/pkg/bft/blockchain/reactor.go: only :269 in respondRoutine, none around ApplyBlock at :536.
candidates.evidence: UPGRADES.md:175 'A node still catching up through block sync ... the process exits with code 2, so a supervisor configured to restart on exit does fire'; reactor.go recover only at :269 (respondRoutine).

candidates.summary: 'start the new version on the same data directory' is unconditional, while the coordinated path the linked UPGRADES.md defines also covers replaying history into a fresh genesis when the state format changes (same text at onyx VALIDATOR.md:149).
candidates.failure_scenario: A future halt whose release changes the state format and ships a new genesis: an operator following section 6 starts the new binary on the old data directory, which replays the last block from the block store (UPGRADES.md:129) instead of starting at InitialHeight from the new genesis, and does not join the new chain until told otherwise by the release notes.
